2. Short facts are that the pre-emptor instituted Miscellaneous Case No.I94 of 1972 under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. 1950 in the First Court of Assistant Judge Laximpur claiming pre-emption of the case land. The contention of the petitioner is that he is a co-sharer by inheritance in the case holding. The opposite party No.2 transferred the case land to the opposite party No.1 by kabala dated 20.06.1972 for a consideration of Tk.400/-. The pre-emptor is not a co-sharer in respect of the land of Khatian Nos.1965 and 1989 as shown in schedule "Ka" to the misc. petition. The pre-emptor is therefore entitled to pre-empt '/ decimals of land in the "Kha" schedule only. No notice of the kabala under pre-emption was served upon the pre-emptor as co-sharer. She for the first time came to learn about kabala under pre-emption on 24.11.1972 after getting certified copy of the same and filed the case within time. 

 3. The pre-emptee contested the case by filing written objection and contended, inter alia that his father Abdus Samad Pandit was a co-sharer in all the Khatians of 'Ka' and 'Kha' schedule case land. Abdus Samad Pandit gifted some lands out of the lands of item No.1 of the 'Kha' schedule land to his third wife opposite Party No.54 by heba-bil-ewaj deed dated 07.10.1988. Abdus Samad Pandit died leaving widow opposite Party No.54 four sons opposite Party Nos.1 and 5-7 and four daughters opposite party Nos.8- 11. In this way the pre-emptee opposite party No.1 is a co-sharer by inheritance in the case holding and as such the case is not maintainable. The further case of the pre-emptee is that he is also a co-sharer by purchase and he got saham for his share in partition suit No.79 of 1970. 

 7. The High Court Division held that the admitted position is that the pre-emptor is a co-sharer by inheritance and no notice of the kabala under pre-emption was served upon her and the case was filed within time. As has already been noticed the trial court allowed the pre-emption in part in respect of land of Khatian Nos.543. 1369. 583. 585 and 2682 and the claim of the pre-emptor in respect of other three khatians was rejected. On appeal the appellate court modified the judgment of the trial court in respect of land of serial Nos.1 and 5 of schedule-'Kha' of the misc. petition. The appellate court further found that the pre-emptee is a co-sharer in respect of the land of serial No.1 of schedule- 1. 'Kha' to the misc. petition the High Court Division accordingly took up for hearing the point as to whether the pre-emptee is also a cu-sharer in respect of the Khatian Nos. 543 and 2682. 

 8. The High Court Division on consideration of the evidence and the material on record specially heba-bil-ewaj deed dated 7.10.1968 Ext.2 executed by Abdus Samad Pandit, father of pre-emptee in favour of his wife Ful Banu, opposite party No.54 came to the conclusion that Abdus Samad Pandit, father of the pre-emptee did not exhaust his entire share in this khatian and accordingly the pre-emptee son of Abdus Samad Pandit is a co-sharer by inheritance. Therefore, the pre-emption is not entitled to get pre-emption of the land of Khatian No.543. Accordingly the High Court Division modified the judgment of the appellate court and trial court and allowed pre-emption in respect of land of khatian No.1369, 583, 585, 1682. The Rule was accordingly made absolute in part.
